sections.heading: Transaction approval
sections.text: Relationship managers may approve SME cross-border transfers within the limits set by the current Cross-Border Payments Standard.

sections.heading: Escalation
sections.text: Transfers above the relationship manager limit require approval from the Business Banking Credit Committee before release.

sections.heading: Relationship manager limit
sections.text: A relationship manager may approve a single SME cross-border transfer of up to SGD 250,000.

sections.heading: Cut-off
sections.text: Transfers approved before 3:00 pm Singapore time are targeted for same-day processing, subject to correspondent bank availability.

sections.heading: Relationship manager limit
sections.text: A relationship manager may approve a single SME cross-border transfer of up to SGD 200,000. This replaces the SGD 250,000 limit in circular DOC-SME-087.

sections.heading: Processing
sections.text: Transfers approved before 2:30 pm Singapore time are targeted for same-day processing. Same-day processing depends on correspondent bank cut-offs.

sections.heading: Beneficial owners
sections.text: Identify every beneficial owner who holds 25% or more of the company's shares or voting rights.

sections.heading: Identity evidence
sections.text: For each beneficial owner, obtain a government-issued photo ID and proof of residential address dated within the last three months.

sections.heading: Company records
sections.text: Obtain the company's latest business profile from the company registry.

sections.heading: Ownership confirmation
sections.text: The ownership structure must be confirmed in writing by a director of the company.

sections.heading: Relationship manager authority
sections.text: Relationship managers may apply FX rate overrides of up to 10 basis points.

sections.heading: Approval above authority
sections.text: Any override above 10 basis points requires prior approval from the Treasury desk head.

sections.heading: Record keeping
sections.text: Every override must be recorded in the deal ticket with a reason code.

sections.heading: Branch manager
sections.text: Branch managers may waive account service fees of up to SGD 500 per account per year.

sections.heading: Area head
sections.text: Waivers above SGD 500 require approval from the area head.

sections.heading: Annual fee reversals
sections.text: Annual fee reversals for retail credit cards are handled by the Cards Service team.

sections.heading: Minimum balance
sections.text: A standard savings account requires an average daily balance of SGD 1,000 in each calendar month.

sections.heading: Fall-below fee
sections.text: A fall-below fee of SGD 2 is charged for any month in which the average daily balance is under SGD 1,000. The fee is waived for account holders aged 21 and below.

sections.heading: Interest
sections.text: Interest is calculated on the end-of-day balance and credited monthly on the last business day of the month.

sections.heading: Dormant accounts
sections.text: An account with no customer-initiated transaction for 24 months is classified as dormant.

sections.heading: Eligibility
sections.text: Individual accounts may be opened by applicants aged 16 and above. Applicants under 18 need a parent or guardian as a joint signatory.

sections.heading: Identity documents — citizens and residents
sections.text: Singapore citizens and permanent residents must provide their NRIC to open an account.

sections.heading: Identity documents — foreigners
sections.text: Foreign applicants must provide a passport, a valid employment or student pass, and proof of residential address dated within the last three months.

sections.heading: Initial deposit
sections.text: An initial deposit of SGD 500 must be made within 30 days of the account being opened.

sections.heading: Politically exposed persons
sections.text: An applicant identified as a politically exposed person needs senior management approval before the account is opened.

DOC-SME-130.title: SME Loan Repayment and Restructuring Guidelines

sections.heading: Grace period
sections.text: A loan repayment received within 7 calendar days of its due date is not treated as late.

sections.heading: Late payment fee
sections.text: After the grace period, a late payment fee of 2% of the overdue instalment is charged, subject to a minimum of SGD 50.

sections.heading: Early repayment
sections.text: A borrower may repay a term loan in full early by giving 30 days' written notice. A prepayment fee of 1.5% of the amount repaid applies during the first two years of the loan.

sections.heading: Restructuring
sections.text: A request to restructure an SME loan must be approved by the Business Banking Credit Committee.

sections.heading: Time limit
sections.text: A customer must raise a card transaction dispute within 60 days of the statement date.

sections.heading: Provisional credit
sections.text: For a dispute above SGD 100, a provisional credit is posted within 10 business days while the case is investigated.

sections.heading: Suspected fraud
sections.text: A suspected fraudulent transaction must be reported immediately, and the card is blocked before the dispute is logged.

sections.heading: Resolution
sections.text: Card disputes are resolved within 90 days of being logged.

sections.heading: Online remittance
sections.text: Overseas remittances made through online banking are charged a flat fee of SGD 10 per transaction.

sections.heading: Branch remittance
sections.text: Overseas remittances made at a branch are charged SGD 30 per transaction.

sections.heading: Online remittance
sections.text: Overseas remittances made through online banking are charged a flat fee of SGD 5 per transaction. This replaces the SGD 10 fee in DOC-REM-014.

sections.heading: Branch remittance
sections.text: Overseas remittances made at a branch are charged SGD 25 per transaction.

sections.heading: Daily limit
sections.text: Online overseas remittances are limited to SGD 50,000 per customer per day.
